knownIssues: Paint opacity is NOT rendered when the paint's color is bound to a variable (Figma renderer limitation, confirmed by sampling exported PNG pixels): use a pre-blended flat solid color instead of variable + opacity for borders/translucent tints.
resize() resets layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical back to FIXED if called after setting AUTO/HUG — set sizing AFTER resize(), not before.

Cannot appendChild into an INSTANCE (only edit nodes that already exist inside it) — reusable slot-less wrappers (StickyHeader/PageContainer) are recomposed inline in composite components instead of being nested as instances.
Icons are generic vector placeholders (not real Lucide icons), exposed via INSTANCE_SWAP on ActionListItem and on Avatar's Icon variant — pending real icon set import / Code Connect.

Appending a new instance into an auto-layout frame with appendChild() puts it LAST in flow, ignoring manually-set x/y — when replacing a child at a specific position (e.g. Card's avatar slot), capture the old child's index and insertChild(index, ...) instead.

Avatar variant 'Size' values (6/8/10/14/24) are Tailwind spacing units, not pixels — actual circle diameter is unit*4px (6→24px ... 24→96px). Caught only after first pass resized components to the raw unit value; fixed by re-resizing all 20 variants.

figma.createNodeFromSvg() + figma.createComponentFromNode() reliably turns a real lucide-static SVG into a proper Figma component — far more accurate than hand-drawing vector placeholders. SVG stroke="currentColor" resolves to flat black; strokes must be manually rebound to a color variable afterward.

Changing an INSTANCE_SWAP property's defaultValue via editComponentProperty() auto-updates every unoverridden instance driven by that property (name + mainComponent), but does NOT preserve the previous instance size/position — it resizes to the new default component's natural size, which can throw off centering (had to re-resize/re-center after every default-value change).

Setting x/y on a deeply-nested child inside an INSTANCE (not the main component) can throw 'This property cannot be overridden in an instance: relative-transform' — happens when that node sits inside an auto-layout ancestor that governs its position; check whether the parent is auto-layout before trying to reposition, since the position is already handled by layout flow (no error, and no fix needed, if so).

Multi-path lucide icons import as MULTIPLE separate VECTOR nodes (one per <path>/<circle>/<line> in the source SVG), not one. Recoloring an icon instance with `iconInst.findOne(n => n.type === 'VECTOR')` only rebinds the FIRST one, leaving the rest at the old color — produces a visibly two-toned icon (e.g. UserPlus's '+' recolored but the person glyph left dark). Always use `findAll`, never `findOne`, when rebinding icon stroke color.

code_connect requires a Dev/Full seat on an Organization or Enterprise Figma plan (not starter/pro) — confirmed via whoami + list_file_components_for_code_connect. Doesn't block anything else; only Dev Mode's code-snippet-next-to-component view is unavailable.

color/border/default was imported WRONG at variable-creation time, not just at a binding site: the real CSS is rgba(58,50,48,0.12) (a 'soft brown border', see app/src/styles/theme.css) but the Figma variable stored the same RGB at alpha=1 — full-opacity near-black instead of a subtle tint. This is the same paint-opacity-ignored-on-variable-bind limitation, but baked into the variable's own stored value rather than at each usage site, so every consumer of this variable rendered a solid black/dark line. Fixed by setValueForMode() to the pre-blended flat solid (blend against color/bg/background, the most common backdrop) — same workaround pattern as other variable+opacity cases. Re-check any OTHER color variable that was originally a translucent rgba() in code for the same bug — this one was caught only because the user compared a real screenshot's Tabbar underline.

StickyHeader (design-system/layouts/StickyHeader.tsx) has its own `border-b border-border` — since StickyHeader is recomposed inline inside PageHeader (per the 'cannot appendChild into an INSTANCE' rule) rather than nested as its own instance, that border has to be manually re-added to every PageHeader variant's own strokes, or it silently disappears. Missed on first pass for both `stacked` and `row` variants; same omission likely worth checking on any other component that inlines StickyHeader/PageContainer's shell instead of nesting it.

Resizing a nested child of an INSTANCE that is a FIXED-size (non-FILL) auto-layout child can silently no-op — no error thrown, but the size just doesn't change (confirmed: `avatarArea.resize(163,163)` on a PersonaCard instance left it at the component's original 160x160, while the outer instance's own resize() DID stick). The reliable fix is to change the size at the COMPONENT definition itself (all instances then inherit it automatically, confirmed working) rather than trying to override geometry on instance children after the fact.

TabButton's active-state underline (bg-primary bar under the label) initially used layoutPositioning='ABSOLUTE' + a manual resize() per instance to match each tab's own text width (Historia/Capítulos/Familia differ) — this hit the exact same silent-no-op as the PersonaCard issue above (every instance stayed frozen at the master's width) AND threw 'cannot be overridden in an instance: relative-transform' when also trying to set x on it. Fixed by making the rectangle an in-flow (non-absolute) auto-layout child with layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' instead — FILL children reliably recompute per-instance (same mechanism used successfully for PersonaCard's nameWrap text), unlike ABSOLUTE overlays or raw resize() overrides on instance children. Costs 2px of extra component height (the underline now occupies its own flow slot instead of overlapping the padding box like CSS `absolute bottom-0`), an acceptable trade-off. Also caught in the same review: TabButton's itemSpacing was 6 (a stray gap between label and underline not present in code, which has no gap — the underline is a zero-flow overlay in CSS), inflating total height to 53px instead of the correct ~47px; set to 0.

After the TabButton height fix (47px), Tabbar's own frame was still a stale counterAxisSizingMode='FIXED' at the height set when it was first built (40px, before TabButton's real height was known) — so the 47px-tall TabButton instances overflowed the declared 40px container, leaving the active tab's underline floating below/disconnected from Tabbar's own border-bottom line instead of flush against it (caught by the user comparing a real screenshot side-by-side). Fixed by setting Tabbar's counterAxisSizingMode='AUTO' (HUG) so its height always tracks its TabButton children's real height exactly — matches code, where Tabbar has no explicit height of its own, it's simply as tall as the tab row inside it. General lesson: any wrapper container built with a fixed height BEFORE its content's final height was known needs re-checking (HUG) once that content changes.

Full-file hygiene pass (user request: check background consistency + overlaps across every page): found and fixed (1) ChapterCard + LooseChapterCard placed at the same (32,40) coordinates already occupied by WorkspaceSwitcherTrigger in Feature Components > Baules — reused a position without checking existing content first; reflowed into a non-overlapping vertical stack and grew the section to fit. (2) IconButton had the exact same primaryAxisSizingMode bug as ExpandableFAB (shrank to 20x40 instead of a fixed 40x40 circle) — invisible in screenshots only because its fill is transparent (no visible tap-target boundary), but still wrong; fixed the same way. (3) Section background fills were inconsistent — Components' section was correctly bound to color/bg/background, but Foundations/Layouts/Screens>Sharing still had Figma's raw default dark-gray section chrome color; normalized every tracked page's sections to the same bound variable. (4) Deleted a leftover 'Uploaded Image' frame on the Components page — the throwaway SVG vector-tree from the beach-photo upload round-trip lands on whatever page is currently active (not the target node's page), so it must be manually cleaned up after every such upload, not just the final PNG re-upload step. Also noted: the file has 4 pre-existing pages unrelated to this workflow (Portada, App, Mesa de trabajo, Descartes) — left untouched, flagged to the user rather than assumed safe to modify.

Icon instances don't auto-scale strokeWeight when resized — unlike a real browser rendering an SVG (where scaling the viewBox via width/height also scales the visual stroke thickness for free), Figma's strokeWeight is a separate absolute px value that resize() does NOT adjust proportionally. Every icon in this file was imported at 24x24 with strokeWeight=2 (matching lucide's real stroke-width:2 at its native viewBox), then placed at many different sizes (12px in ChapterCard's counts, 20px in most buttons, 40px in PersonaCard, 80px in EmptyState...) via plain resize() — leaving the stroke visually too thick at small sizes and it would look too thin if any master were ever built larger, since strokeWeight stayed frozen at 2 everywhere. Fixed by sweeping every page (Components/Layouts/Feature Components) for INSTANCE nodes whose mainComponent name starts with 'Icon/' and setting each one's VECTOR children's strokeWeight = 2 * (instance.width / 24) — i.e. proportional to its own actual placed size, not the master's. This must be re-applied any time a NEW icon instance is placed at a non-24px size — there's no automatic mechanism for it, it's a manual step after every resize().

ExpandableFAB was built without an explicit primaryAxisSizingMode='FIXED' on the auto-layout frame, so after appendChild(icon) the frame HUGged down to the icon's own 24px width instead of staying a fixed 56x56 circle (counterAxisSizingMode was already 'FIXED', but that only governs the cross axis in a HORIZONTAL frame — the primary/width axis defaulted to AUTO). Fixed by explicitly setting primaryAxisSizingMode='FIXED' then resize(56,56) again. General lesson: for any circular icon-only button (FAB, IconButton), set BOTH primaryAxisSizingMode and counterAxisSizingMode to 'FIXED' explicitly — don't rely on one of them defaulting correctly.

TabButton's underline is a `border-bottom`-style element (spans the ENTIRE button edge-to-edge, not just the label text), and needed two more rounds after the HUG fix: (1) the frame's own paddingBottom (14px, from py-3.5) still sat AFTER the underline in flow, leaving a 14px gap below it instead of the line sitting flush at the true bottom edge — fixed by zeroing paddingBottom and moving that 14px into itemSpacing (12px gap + 2px line = 14px, so height stays correct at 45px, matching code's real total, while the line itself now touches the bottom edge). (2) the underline's layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' was filling only the CONTENT box (frame width minus the 4px+4px horizontal padding, i.e. narrower than the full button) since that same padding was on the same frame as the underline — fixed by moving the horizontal px-1 padding onto a new inner 'Label' wrapper around just the text, leaving the outer TabButton frame's own horizontal padding at 0 so the FILL-width underline now spans the button's true full width edge-to-edge, matching a real CSS border-bottom rather than a text-underline.

An imageHash already known-good on one fill (obtained via the upload_assets SVG→PNG→re-upload round-trip) CAN be reused directly on a brand-new node's fills array in a plain use_figma script (fills = [{type:'IMAGE', scaleMode:'FILL', imageHash}]) — no need to re-run upload_assets per node. Confirmed working when applying Avatar's already-uploaded photo hash to 4 new PersonaCard instances in one script.

SimpleFAB/ExpandableFAB are 'fixed bottom-6 right-5' in real code — right-aligned to the screen edge, NOT horizontally centered. All 3 Baul screens' FABs had been positioned centered (a mistake carried over from the first BaulPersonasScreen build and copied to the other 2) — user caught it as looking 'pocho'/off. Fixed by recomputing x = screen.x + screen.width - 20 - fab.width, y = screen.y + screen.height - 24 - fab.height for all 3 (BaulPersonasScreen's SimpleFAB, BaulCapitulosScreen's ExpandableFAB, BaulRecuerdosScreen's SimpleFAB). Also worth checking: BaulRecuerdosScreen's screen frame height must be read AFTER its auto-layout Body has settled (it grows from the feed cards), not a stale/assumed value, or the FAB's y ends up floating below the screen's real bottom edge.

Tailwind responsive classes encode a MOBILE-FIRST breakpoint order — `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3` means 2 columns is the base/mobile layout and 3 only applies at `sm:` (640px) and up. Since these screens are built at real mobile frame widths (390px), always use the base (unprefixed) class, not the largest one — building `sm:grid-cols-3` here was a first-pass mistake caught by the user comparing against a real screenshot at phone width.

Building a vertical (top-to-bottom) linear gradient paint requires a manual gradientTransform matrix — there is no simple angle/direction property. Formula used: given desired gradient handles start=(0.5,0) end=(0.5,1) width-axis=(1,0) in normalized node space, gradientTransform = [[end.x-start.x, widthAxis.x-start.x, start.x], [end.y-start.y, widthAxis.y-start.y, start.y]] = [[0,0.5,0.5],[1,0,0]] for Hero's bg-gradient-to-t overlay. A first guess of [[0,1,0],[-1,0,1]] produced a diagonal/near-opaque mess instead of a clean vertical fade — verified only by screenshot, not inferable from the API types.

PageHeader's row variant already ships default Leading (WorkspaceSwitcherTrigger) and Trailing (IconButton -> Icon/menu) instances baked into the master — for a screen that needs a plain BackButton + a different trailing icon (e.g. ChapterRoute, unlike BaulRoute), swap those existing instances' mainComponent in place (leading.mainComponent = BackButtonComp, trailingIcon.mainComponent = otherIconComp) rather than trying to appendChild a new node into the Trailing slot — appendChild into an INSTANCE still throws 'New parent is an instance or is inside of an instance' even for a frame that looks like an empty slot, because it isn't empty, it already holds a default instance to swap instead of replace.

A parent auto-layout frame's primaryAxisSizingMode/counterAxisSizingMode set to AUTO (hug) BEFORE that frame's own resize() call gets silently reset back to FIXED by that resize() call (same root cause as the already-documented resize()-resets-sizing-mode issue, but this time hit on a plain container frame — ChapterFotosScreen's Body — not a component, so it was easy to miss: the frame LOOKED like it should hug because AUTO was set, but a resize(390,100) placeholder call two lines later silently undid it, and the bug was invisible until a second use_figma call re-measured body.height and still got the stale placeholder value. Fixed by re-setting primaryAxisSizingMode = 'AUTO' again AFTER all content was appended (no further resize() calls after that point) rather than before.

No existing color variable is scoped for a FRAME_FILL dark-surface / TEXT_FILL light-text inversion (PhotoViewer's bg-foreground-over-text-background surface) — color/text/foreground is TEXT_FILL-only. Used flat pre-blended solid colors (no variable binding) for the whole PhotoViewerScreen family instead of introducing a new variable for a single-screen use case; revisit if a second dark-surface screen shows up.

photoViewerManyTagsNote: PhotoViewerScreen (Mobile, muchas etiquetas) (229:514), user request: mobile variant with several tagged-persona badges wrapping to ~3 lines - models the taggedPersonas.length > 0 flex-wrap gap-2 branch in PhotoViewer.tsx with enough PersonBadge instances (7: Abuela Rosa with a real photo avatar, Papa, Mama, Marta, Tio Carlos, Prima Lucia, Yo) in a layoutWrap=WRAP frame to actually wrap 3 rows at 342px width, instead of the single-badge case built for the other PhotoViewer screens. Hit the resize()-resets-AUTO-sizing-mode gotcha yet again on the wrap frame itself (counterAxisSizingMode was set to AUTO before an initial placeholder resize() call, silently reverting it to FIXED at the old 32px single-row height and causing the Recuerdos card below to overlap rows 2-3) - fixed the same way as ChapterFotosScreen, by re-setting counterAxisSizingMode = 'AUTO' again after all 7 badges were appended.
